title: 2026 Outputs: Status and Q4 Plan
summary: At the pace of the first nine months only 4 of 14 measurable outputs reach target by 31 December; delivering the Priority 1 and 2 aims would raise that to 8.

headline.label: Measurable targets met at current pace
Met if Priority 1 and 2 are delivered

breakdowns.title: Status of the 25 annual outputs at 30 September

highlights: Q4 plan: five outputs can still close by 31 December — monitoring reports, fumigation, polluted sites, lab accreditation, handler training

challenges.text: Vehicles and fuel — unlocks outputs 6, 4, 22, 17 and 8
PPE for chemical handlers — needed for trainings and inventories
Computers and a printer — unlocks waste certificates and faster report reviews
Regulatory sign-off — publish the radiation regulation and Schedule 5 fees
Staff — six laboratory posts (output 5) remain unfilled

actions.text: Monitoring reports: 13 more, with written deadlines for late proponents
Fumigation licences: 2 more — call pending applicants trained in Bong County
Polluted sites: restore 2 more, e.g. Monrovia Industrial Park
Lab accreditation: inspect and accredit 5 more operator laboratories
Two handler trainings: Freeport with NPA, and mining reagent handlers
Disposal licences: identify holders of obsolete chemicals and invite 5 to apply
Effluent licences: 10 more from dischargers already known
Waste licences: clear the backlog, print certificates weekly (15 more)
National radiation safety training for 50 medical radiographers
Waste mapping: register 30 generators met during ESIA visits
Radiation inventory: 15 more facilities in Montserrado and Margibi
Chemical inventory: start school laboratories, add Monrovia industrial sites
Draft one paper from a 2026 dataset, e.g. the noise study

milestones.text: Unit heads report October results; logistics request to management
Second check: both trainings and lab accreditations done
Q4 and annual report; carry outputs 22, 6 and 4 into 2027
